---
title: "Supported documents"
description: "Choose the documents your customers can capture."
---

The SDK supplies available countries and documents for your integration. Use those choices to build your selectors; they reflect your organization’s and venue’s capture settings.

## Document types

| Document | Issuing countries | What the customer captures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Driver’s license | United States, Canada | Back with a readable PDF417 barcode; front when requested |
| State or provincial ID | United States, Canada | Back with a readable PDF417 barcode; front when requested |
| Passport | Available issuing countries | Full photo page, including the machine-readable text at the bottom |
| Passport card | United States | Side containing the machine-readable text |
| Permanent resident card | United States, Canada | Side containing the supported machine-readable text |
| Visa | Available issuing countries | Visa page containing the machine-readable text |
| Other travel document | Available issuing countries | Document page or side containing a supported machine-readable zone |

Enhanced driver’s licenses appear under **Driver’s license**. Country selection refers to the document’s issuing country.

## Restrict accepted documents

Configure document restrictions for your organization or venue. For example, a passport-only flow shows passport choices; a driver’s-license flow offers countries where that document is supported.

The SDK provides `countryCodes` and `allowedDocumentTypes` after authorization. Refresh the document choices when the customer changes country. See [Customize capture](/external/customize#choose-documents-before-opening-the-camera).

## Capture one or both sides

Enable `dual_document_capture` in the venue’s preferences to request the front of an ID after its barcode side. Passports use their photo page. Read the SDK’s required sides to display the current instruction.

## Barcode and MRZ formats

ID capture reads supported PDF417 barcodes. Travel-document capture reads the machine-readable zone (MRZ), the block of letters, digits, and `<` characters printed on the document.

| MRZ format | Printed layout | Typical document |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TD1 | 3 lines, 30 characters each | Travel and identity cards |
| TD2 | 2 lines, 36 characters each | Travel documents |
| TD3 | 2 lines, 44 characters each | Passports |
| MRV-A | 2 lines, 44 characters each | Visas |
| MRV-B | 2 lines, 36 characters each | Visas |

Ask the customer to keep the complete document and machine-readable text in view. For a document without a supported barcode or MRZ, offer another accepted document.
